newsitem.title: USA: ISS supports vote for Sallie Mae dissidents.
newsitem.headline: ISS supports vote for Sallie Mae dissidents.

text.p: Institutional Shareholder Services, a firm which advises institutional shareholders on how to vote in proxy contests, Thursday recommended a vote for a slate of directors nominated by the Committee To Restore Value (CRV), a group opposing the management of Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae).

On July 31, shareholders are scheduled to vote on a plan to privatize Sallie Mae and end its status as a government sponsored enterprise. Shareholders will also choose between a slate of directors backed by the current management of Sallie Mae or the rival slate of the CRV.

According to the CRV, ISS said it favors the CRV's strategic focus, sensitivity to shareholder value, and management team. ISS said the current Sallie Mae management has "managed to keep the Sallie Mae ship afloat, but it has not demonstrated that it can do so without the CRV on board."
A group of CRV directors were elected to the Sallie Mae board in 1995 on a platform centered on the enhancement of shareholder value.
Albert Lord, a former Sallie Mae chief operating officer and chief financial officer, would become chief executive should the CRV slate win the election.
